variant_desc: 64M-double (512MB) buffer: serial init then parallel-sum (slow) -> parallel first-touch init then same-partition parallel-sum (fast) (variant 4: seed=46, n_scale=0.7x)
source_citation: ggerganov/llama.cpp issue #12759 (filed 2025-04-04, ~17% throughput loss from non-NUMA-aware allocation): https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/issues/12759
novelty_rationale: Tests recognition that page placement is established at FIRST write under Linux's first-touch NUMA policy, so the threads that will later READ a page must also be the threads that INIT it. Compilers cannot perform this because page placement is an OS-level allocation-time decision driven by which CPU faulted the page in, invisible to any compile-time analysis. NOTE: on non-NUMA hardware (Apple Silicon, single-socket) the only visible speedup comes from parallel zeroing bandwidth; on actual 2-socket NUMA boxes the pattern recovers the ~17% LLM-inference throughput loss documented in the cited issue.
